about: The AP Physics 1 app pages. scripts/build-apphys.mjs writes each page's shell (head, header, footer, a <div id="app"> mount) from this file; the page's behavior is its script in physics/assets/<script>, which mounts into #app. "static": true marks a generated page that is not an app (teachers.html). premium names the Premium feature (ApPhysCore gates it); card is the line on the course home. No path may contain the token "ap" (docs/apphys-spec.md decision 2). tools[] are the eleven trainers of docs/apphys-spec.md section 6, pre-registered in Phase 0: page physics/tools/<slug>.html, script physics/assets/tools/<slug>.js, model physics/assets/tools/math/<slug>.js (ApPhysMath.<camelSlug>), content physics/data/tools/<slug>.json, validator scripts/lib/apphys-tool-checks/<slug>.mjs, test scripts/test/apphys-tool-<slug>.test.mjs (docs/apphys-architecture.md, "Tools"). topic is the tool's context topic: the tool is built only when its data file exists and that topic is published. Free or Premium: motion-graphs, free-body-diagrams and scaling-drills are free; the rest carry "premium": "tools" (docs/apphys-spec.md decision on free trainers; owner to confirm).

apps.title: Practice questions
apps.desc: Physics practice by unit, topic or skill: stimulus sets, scene diagrams and calculations graded on value, units and sig figs, with every option explained.
apps.card: Drill a unit, a topic or a science practice, with stimulus sets.

apps.title: Spaced review
apps.desc: Your physics spaced review queue: every question you missed comes back just before you would forget it.
apps.card: Missed questions come back when you are about to forget them.

apps.title: Unit tests and practice exams
apps.desc: Timed physics unit tests and full practice exams in the real format: 42 multiple-choice questions in 85 minutes, then 4 free-response questions in 95.
apps.card: Unit tests and full timed practice exams in the real 42 + 4 format.

apps.title: Free-response practice
apps.desc: Physics free-response practice in the four exam types, each with a point-by-point rubric, a full-credit sample answer and a printable answer sheet.
apps.card: All four free-response types, with rubrics and sample answers.

apps.title: Justification trainer
apps.desc: Physics explain and justify practice: write an answer, check it against a rubric, and compare an answer that earns the point with one that does not.
apps.lede: Write an explain or justify answer, then check it against the rubric and two model answers.
apps.card: Explain and justify prompts with a rubric checklist and two model answers.

apps.title: Cram kit
apps.desc: Physics cram plans counted back from your exam date: three or two weeks, day by day, weighted by unit, with unit sheets, timed mixed sets and practice exams.
apps.lede: A 3-week or 2-week plan counted back from your exam date, day by day: unit sheets and notes, a timed mixed set and one free-response question each study day, two full practice exams and rest days. Print it and tick the days off.
apps.card: 3-week and 2-week plans to exam day, and timed mixed sets.

apps.title: Flashcards
apps.desc: Spaced-repetition physics flashcards built from the glossary, by unit and topic.

apps.title: Trainers and drills
apps.desc: Physics trainers: free-body diagrams, motion graphs, energy bar charts, collisions, torque, oscillators, fluids and lab design, each followed by questions.
apps.card: Trainers and drills, then the questions about what you did.

apps.title: Your dashboard
apps.desc: Your physics mastery by unit, topic and science practice, with every miss linked to the lesson that teaches it.
apps.card: Mastery by unit, topic and science practice.

apps.title: Search the course
apps.desc: Search every physics lesson, notes page, glossary term and tool in the course.

apps.title: For teachers
apps.desc: For physics teachers: stable share links, printable notes and unit sheets, and sharing pages to Google Classroom, with no new student data collected.
apps.lede: Share any notes page, lesson or unit sheet with a stable link. Students need no account, and nothing they do leaves their device unless they choose to sign in.

tools.name: Scaling drills
tools.title: Scaling and units drills
tools.desc: Unlimited functional-dependence and units drills: if the length is four times as long, how does the period change? Seeded, checked step by step.
tools.blurb: How a quantity scales when another doubles, triples or halves, and units that cancel.
tools.lede: Predict how one quantity changes when another is scaled.

tools.name: Motion graphs
tools.title: Motion graphs trainer
tools.desc: Drive a cart along a track and watch its position, velocity and acceleration graphs draw live; read slopes and areas and match motions to graphs.
tools.blurb: Drive a cart and watch x, v and a draw themselves; read slope and area.
tools.lede: Drive a cart and watch its motion graphs draw themselves.

tools.name: Lab design
tools.title: Experimental design trainer
tools.desc: Experimental design practice: what to measure with which instrument, what to plot for a straight line, and what the slope means, with seeded noisy data.
tools.blurb: What to measure with what, what to plot for a straight line, and what the slope means.
tools.lede: Plan a measurement, linearize the data and read the slope.

tools.name: Projectile lab
tools.title: Projectile lab
tools.desc: Launch a projectile at any angle and speed: velocity components, trajectory, time of flight and range, and the same motion seen from a moving frame.
tools.blurb: Launch at any angle and speed; components, range and time of flight.
tools.lede: Launch a ball and see its motion split into two.

tools.name: Free-body diagrams
tools.title: Free-body diagram builder
tools.desc: Drag forces onto a block on an incline, a hanging mass, an elevator or a car on a curve; each force graded, with extra, missing and wrong forces named.
tools.blurb: Drag and size the forces on real scenes; each force graded, every miss named.
tools.lede: Draw the forces on an object and see if they add up.

tools.name: Energy bar charts
tools.title: Energy bar chart trainer
tools.desc: Watch energy move between kinetic, gravitational and spring energy on a skater track, a launcher and a rough ramp, then build the bar charts.
tools.blurb: Skater track, spring launcher and rough ramp, with live energy bars.
tools.lede: Watch energy change form, then build the bar charts yourself.

tools.name: Collision lab
tools.title: Collision lab
tools.desc: Two carts on a track, from elastic to sticky: momentum and energy bar charts before and after, and the force-time graph with its impulse.
tools.blurb: Elastic to sticky collisions with momentum and energy bars, and impulse.
tools.lede: Crash two carts and see what is conserved.

tools.name: Torque balance
tools.title: Torque balance trainer
tools.desc: Hang masses on a beam or a mobile and balance the torques; lever arms, rotational equilibrium, and a race between shapes with different rotational inertia.
tools.blurb: Balance a beam with masses; lever arms, torques and rotational inertia.
tools.lede: Hang masses on a beam and make it balance.

tools.name: Rotation lab
tools.title: Rotation lab
tools.desc: A rolling race down a ramp, a spinning skater who pulls in her arms, and a satellite on an orbit: rotational energy and angular momentum, live.
tools.blurb: Rolling races, a spinning skater and orbit energy.
tools.lede: Race shapes down a ramp and spin a skater.

tools.name: Oscillator lab
tools.title: Oscillator lab
tools.desc: A mass on a spring and a pendulum: position, velocity and acceleration graphs, energy as it sloshes back and forth, and what sets the period.
tools.blurb: Spring and pendulum: graphs, energy, and what sets the period.
tools.lede: Set a mass bouncing and find what changes its period.

tools.name: Fluids tank
tools.title: Fluids tank
tools.desc: Drop objects of different density into a tank, read pressure at any depth, and push fluid through a narrowing pipe to see continuity and Bernoulli at work.
tools.blurb: Buoyancy, pressure with depth and flow through a pipe.
tools.lede: Drop objects in a tank and see what floats and why.
